scope: Version the current call-row task to disclose its existing closed replacement syntax and correct byte-versus-token planning for that new version, preserving historical requests and existing authority boundaries.
riskAnalysis: New paid-task scope and token admission are security sensitive. Keep old policies/requests/spent approval immutable, require exact authenticated input counting before Responses, maintain bounded wire bytes and all token/call/output/time ceilings, serial grants, cleanup and proposal-only authority.

threatModel.assets: Task/source/release identity, old receipts, dedicated credentials, request/token accounting and disposable copy integrity.
threatModel.trustBoundaries: Trusted frozen syntax metadata versus untrusted model output; serialized wire bytes versus authenticated provider token counts; Work owner activation versus internal proposal-only roles.
threatModel.abuseCases: Treating grammar as execution authority; forged descriptor/policy or stale grant; using byte planning to bypass exact counts; parallel trials/retries; losing historical request reconstruction; claiming fixture or automated review as live acceptance.
threatModel.mitigations: Separate frozen descriptor and explicit policy; oldv1hash preserved; unchanged backend grammar, schema identities and source preimage; shared bounded wire ceiling plus actual count gate, per-call and aggregate bounds; exact release configuration, canonical journal, serial grants and cleanup; no test profile/publication authority.

defects.rootCause: The model-facing scope omitted the exact replacement grammar enforced by the backend, and the legacy rehearsal planner compared serialized bytes with a token ceiling.
defects.detectionGap: Schema-valid proposals could fail an undisclosed constraint; compact byte-based fixtures did not reflect the real restricted-worker context. Historical rejected text is unavailable, so no claim that it was a false positive.
defects.regression: All-five actual-controller and restricted-worker fixtures; explicit grammar metadata/no fixture answer, wire-versus-token characterization,12000x5inclusive/12001beforeResponses, replay/cleanup and cross-version substitution. Frozen all10 historical request hashes plus both actual prior paid hashes reconstruct exactly.
defects.historicalPrevention: Use explicit versioned task contracts with shared transport-byte constants and independently counted token ceilings; freeze all-stage request reconstruction before changes, and run source-bound engineering preflight before every push.

rollback: Disable paid authority and future flags, revoke temporary grants, stop the sequence and verify cleanup. Preserve old/new descriptor recognition, policy definitions, receipts, accounting and failed evidence; no history rewrite or Production action. Revert feature behavior only through reviewed exact successor releases.
